transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you so much for seeing me, Doctor. I hope I'm not wasting your time... is it alright if I just explain what's been happening? 

I, um... I've been having a little trouble lately with my eating at night. It's probably silly, I know a woman my age should have much better self-control. But... I'll have these nights where I just eat, and then I sit there with crumbs and empty wrappers and containers all around me. And, oh, I hope you don't judge me too harshly for this, but I feel just so... ashamed. So disgusted with myself. 

It's really why I finally made the appointment. It's gotten to where the next morning, I feel so terrible about it all that I can hardly even bring myself to pray... or look any of the good folks at church in the eye. I just feel so embarrassed. Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be coming to you for? I hope I'm in the right place.
When you're eating at night like that, do you feel like you can stop whenever you want?

Oh, well... I'd like to think I could. I really try to be good, I promise I do. But... to be perfectly honest with you—and I feel so silly admitting this—once I take that very first bite after the house gets completely quiet... it's like my good sense just steps aside. 

Even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now, you've had plenty,' my... my hands just keep reaching for more. It's like I just can't make myself put it away, even though I want to. I know a woman my age should be much stronger than that. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating and how much you're eating during those nights?

Oh, I suppose that's what I was trying to explain just a moment ago, Doctor. I really wish I could tell you yes, that I'm completely in charge of it all. I know a grown woman should be. 

But... no. Like I was saying, it just feels like I lose my grip on it entirely. I'll end up eating things I didn't even plan to touch, and just... keep going and going, even when my mind is begging me to put it away. It's like I'm just watching myself do it and I can't step on the brakes, no matter how much I want to. 

I'm so sorry if I'm just repeating myself now, I don't mean to talk your ear off in circles... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right. Am I being helpful at all?
Do you feel guilty while you're eating at night, or is the guilt something that comes afterwards?

Well... it's a little bit of both, I suppose, but it's really the *afterward* that's the hardest part. I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic. 

While I'm eating, I do feel a little bad, because I know I shouldn't be doing it... but it's when I finally stop, and I look around at the mess. Like I mentioned before, I'll just be sitting there with all those empty wrappers and containers and crumbs everywhere. And the shame just washes over me. It's just so awful, Doctor. 

I feel so disgusted with myself. That's the part that really lingers, you know? It carries right over into the next day, making me feel so unworthy that I can't even find the words to pray, or look my friends at church in the eye. I just feel like such a fraud around all those good people. 

I hope that answers your question properly. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed any issues with your sex life or sexual desire around the same time as these eating episodes?

Oh, my... well. Um... no, I can't say that I have. To be completely honest with you, Doctor, at my age, that's... well, it's just not really an active part of my life anymore anyway. So I certainly haven't noticed any changes or problems with that at all. 

I hope it's alright to just leave it at that. I wouldn't want to skip over anything if it's important for your notes, but... no, nothing like that has been bothering me. Is that the kind of answer you needed, or did I misunderstand the question?
Do you usually feel hungry when you start eating at night?

Well, um... no, not really. That's the strange part about it, I suppose. I'm usually not hungry at all when it starts. 

I mean, I'll have already eaten my dinner, so my stomach is perfectly full. But I just... I just eat anyway. It's almost like a nervous habit, maybe? I hope that doesn't make me sound completely foolish, eating when I'm not even hungry. I know it's a terrible waste of food, and I feel just awful about that part of it too. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I'm trying my best to explain it right, but I know it must sound so silly to someone like you who understands how these things are supposed to work. Am I giving you the right information?
Do you ever try to make up for these nighttime eating episodes by restricting your food intake or purging the next day?

Oh, no... no, I don't do anything like that. I know some people might do those things, but I could never. 

I mean, I'll sometimes tell myself the next morning that I should just have a lighter breakfast, maybe just a piece of toast, since I had so much the night before. But I don't... I don't starve myself or anything extreme like that. And I certainly don't throw up or take pills or anything. That just seems so dangerous, and I wouldn't want to cause any trouble for my health. 

I just try to wake up and have a normal day, even though I feel so terribly guilty. I hope that's the right thing to do? I mean, I know the nighttime eating is wrong, but I try not to make it worse the next day. Is that what you were hoping to hear, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you experienced any difficulty with sexual arousal or pleasure during the times when you haven't been having these nighttime eating episodes?

Oh, dear... um. Well, like I think I mentioned just a little bit ago, Doctor, that's... that's really just not a part of my day-to-day life anymore. At my age, it's just not something I'm active with. 

So, no, I haven't noticed any difficulties with arousal or anything like that, because it's just not happening at all, whether I'm having the eating episodes or not. 

I hope I'm not being unhelpful by saying the same thing again! I really don't mean to be difficult. I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you the right answers for your evaluation. Did I explain that okay, or is there something more specific you need me to think about?
Do you usually feel like you're eating quickly during those nighttime episodes?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose I do eat rather quickly. I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, honestly. It's not very ladylike, is it? 

When I'm standing there at the kitchen counter, I just... I eat so fast that I barely even taste what I'm having. It could be pound cake or a box of crackers, and I just sort of rush through it. Sometimes I even catch myself swallowing before I've rightly chewed my food. It's awful, I know. 

I try to tell myself to slow down and sit at the table like a normal person, but in the moment, it just happens so fast. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for that. I know it's a terrible habit. Is that... is that the sort of thing you needed to know, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that's definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar time period during these nighttime episodes?

Oh, goodness... well... I suppose it might be, yes. I'm so embarrassed to even admit this out loud, Doctor, I really am. I try to tell myself I'm just having a little snack, but... well, on a bad night, it can add up to quite a bit. 

Like, I might start with a plate of leftover funeral-luncheon casserole, just thinking a few bites will settle me. But then, before I even really know what's happening, I've eaten all of that, and... well, maybe half a pan of brownies, some biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is sitting in the fridge. Just... all in one sitting. 

I know that's much more than a normal person would have, isn't it? I feel just terrible telling you this, it sounds so out of control. I hope you don't think awfully of me for it. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth so you have what you need for your notes. Did I answer that right for you?
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen?

Oh, um... well, it's... it's a bit frequent, I suppose. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, but... well, since my dear friend passed away, it seems to be happening more often. 

I'd say these little late-night spells happen at least once or twice most weeks. And, um, honestly, there hasn't really been a month where they've completely let up since then. I try so hard to be good and just stay in bed, but it's been a struggle. 

I know I should be doing better at my age, handling my grief without turning to the pantry. I hope that's not too disappointing to hear. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for, Doctor? I want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these nighttime episodes?

Oh, dear... well... yes, I suppose that's a fair way to put it. I feel so silly even saying this out loud, but... once the house gets all quiet and I take that very first bite, it's almost like... like my good sense just steps aside. 

I'll be standing there, and in my head I'm telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now, you've had enough,' but... my hands just keep reaching for more. It's like I just can't make myself turn around and put the food away, no matter how much I want to be good. 

I try so hard to be strong-willed, I really do. I hope you don't think I'm just terribly weak for not being able to stop myself. Is that... does that make sense, Doctor? Am I explaining it the way you need for your evaluation?
Do you usually feel guilty or self-critical after one of these nighttime eating episodes?

Oh, goodness... well, yes. Yes, I do. I almost didn't even make this appointment because I was just so... so ashamed to talk about it. 

I try to just put it out of my mind, but... when it's all over, and I'm just sitting there in the kitchen with the crumbs and the empty containers all around me... oh, Doctor, I just feel so disgusted with myself. It's an awful, heavy feeling. It gets so bad that I can hardly even bring myself to pray, and... well, looking the folks at church in the eye the next morning is just terribly hard. I feel like they can see right through me, like they know what a mess I am.

I know I shouldn't let myself get so worked up over it, and I'm sorry to be such a bother with all these sad feelings. I just want to be a good patient and give you the honest truth. Is that... is that the sort of thing you needed to know for your notes? I hope I'm not oversharing or making things difficult for you.
Do you feel like you're eating in response to an emotional state, such as stress or anxiety, when these episodes happen?

Oh, hmm... well, I'm honestly not entirely sure. I hope it's alright to say that. 

I know I mentioned missing my dear friend earlier, but... when I actually get out of bed and go to the kitchen, I don't think I'm feeling stressed or anxious. At least, I haven't really noticed feeling that way right in that moment. It's more just... the house is so quiet, and I just find myself doing it. I don't feel all worked up or panicky or anything like that. 

I'm so sorry, I wish I had a better answer for you. I just don't want to mislead you or say the wrong thing. Is it... is it okay that I don't really know exactly what I'm feeling when it starts? I can try to think a little harder on it if that's what you need for your notes, Doctor.
Do you feel like you're unable to control how much you're eating once you start during these episodes?

Oh, dear... well, I suppose that's very similar to what we were just talking about, isn't it? 

I... yes, I think that's true. Once I start, I really do lose track of how much I'm having. I'll think I'm just going to have a little taste of something, just a tiny bit to settle myself, but then... well, before I know it, the whole package is just gone. 

I don't mean to do it, I really don't. I know a lady my age ought to have better manners and more self-restraint than that. I just... I can't seem to rein it in once the ball gets rolling, so to speak. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, Doctor. I know you asked something quite like this just a moment ago. Am I... am I giving you the right kind of details? I just want to make sure I'm being a good help to you.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your eating once you've started during these nighttime episodes?

Oh, my... well, I know we just touched on this, and I feel terrible making you ask again. I hope I wasn't being unclear before. 

But yes, Doctor... it's exactly like that. Once I take that very first bite, especially when the house is all quiet, it's just like... like my good sense completely steps aside. Even while I'm sitting there, literally telling myself, 'Belinda, you need to stop right now,' my hands just... they just keep reaching for more. It's like I can't make them listen to me.

It sounds so foolish when I say it out loud. A woman my age should be in charge of her own hands, shouldn't she? I do try my very best to be good, I promise. I hope that makes sense... is that the kind of explanation you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your actions once you start eating at night?

Oh, dear... I feel like I'm taking up so much of your time with the same sort of answer, and I am truly sorry if I'm making you repeat yourself, Doctor. I know you're very busy.

But... yes, it really is just as I was saying. It's like I completely lose the steering wheel once I start. I know I shouldn't, and I really do try to be mindful, but the control just... slips away. I don't mean to be difficult, I really don't. Am I... am I answering this the right way for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
How often do you feel guilty or self-critical after one of these nighttime eating episodes?

Oh, my... well, I... I suppose I feel that way quite a bit. I really don't like to admit it, Doctor, because I know I ought to be more positive and count my blessings. 

But... oh, it's just dreadful. After it happens, I'll just sit there in the quiet, looking at all the crumbs and the empty containers, and I just feel so... so ashamed. I feel just disgusted with myself, to be perfectly honest. It gets so bad that the next morning, I can hardly even bring myself to pray, or look the folks at church in the eye. I just feel like such a failure, letting myself go like that. 

I know I shouldn't let it get me down so much, and I try to keep a cheerful face on for everyone else. I hope it's alright that I'm sharing this with you... I know it's not a very pretty picture. Does that... does that help you understand what I'm going through? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
